title: The Case for the Unified Agentic Core in Insurance
gist: BCG argues insurers scaling agentic AI should choose a unified agentic core — deterministic and agentic components on one AI-native stack — over bolting AI onto legacy cores or a 'skinny core', citing commercial P&C underwriting cycles cut from 10-20 days to 1-2 and 70%-90% straight-through claims. Success requires a three-tier orchestration hierarchy driven by an executable process blueprint and an in-house, governed insurance data ontology, and BCG warns against waiting for vendors like Guidewire and Duck Creek, saying the window is months, not years.

insights.claim: Based on BCG experience, agentic AI in commercial property and casualty insurance can cut underwriting cycles from 10-20 days to 1-2 days.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude speedup in underwriting turnaround implies quote-speed becomes a competitive weapon in commercial P&C.
insights.quote: can drastically cut underwriting cycles from 10 to 20 days to 1 to 2 days

insights.claim: Agentic AI can raise straight-through claims processing to 70%-90% and contribute to a material improvement in insurers' loss ratios.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Loss-ratio and expense-ratio improvement from claims automation is a direct earnings lever for carriers that scale first.
insights.quote: significant increase in straight-through processing of up to 70% to 90%
insights.locator: By now, most insurance companies are

insights.claim: Insurance is especially exposed to AI disruption because it is among the most data-intensive industries, and the question for COOs and CIOs has shifted from what agentic AI can do to how to transform the core system to scale it.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The bottleneck for AI value in insurance is core-system architecture, not model capability, favoring spend on core modernization.
insights.quote: insurance is especially exposed because it is among the most data intensive
insights.locator: AI is reshaping every industry, but

insights.claim: BCG frames three archetypes for integrating agentic AI into insurance core systems: existing core plus agentic platform, 'skinny core' plus agentic platform, and a unified agentic core, each with a different pace of value capture and transformation risk.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Provides a lens to classify carriers' and vendors' AI strategies by durability versus speed-to-value.
insights.locator: The Three Archetypes for Core Modernization

insights.claim: Keeping the legacy core and adding an agentic layer is the fastest, least disruptive route to impact, but legacy and integration complexity cap the benefits and duplicate orchestration layers accumulate over time.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Carriers taking the bolt-on route may show early wins but face compounding technical debt and rising run costs later.
insights.quote: duplicate orchestration layers tend to build up over time
insights.locator: Existing Core Plus Agentic Platform

insights.claim: A skinny core moves customer interaction, workflow orchestration, business rules, automated decisioning, document processing and partner orchestration to the agentic platform, while raw data, financial processing, reinsurance accounting, regulatory reporting and the audit trail remain in the core.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Signals which core functions remain sticky for incumbent core vendors and which migrate to agentic platforms.
insights.locator: Skinny Core Plus Agentic Platform

insights.claim: The unified agentic core designs deterministic core and agentic capabilities as a single AI-native stack, offering the most future-proof architecture at the cost of the highest effort, risk, engineering capacity needs and longest path to value.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Implies a multi-year capex and engineering-talent commitment for carriers choosing this path, with delayed but more durable returns.
insights.quote: core and agents designed as one system rather than two
insights.locator: Unified Agentic Core.

insights.claim: Contrary to the appeal of quick bolt-on gains, BCG argues only the unified agentic core solves underlying integration problems; the alternatives deliver a temporary productivity boost while adding extra layers to the existing landscape.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Productivity gains from AI layers on legacy cores may prove transient, a caution when valuing early AI-driven efficiency claims.
insights.quote: only the unified agentic core solves the underlying integration problems with existing systems and data platforms
insights.locator: Making the Case for the Unified Agentic Core

insights.claim: BCG claims a unified agentic core yields faster iteration via a single configuration point, shared learning from the same data assets as transactional processing, lower run costs from fewer redundant high-availability layers, and embedded end-to-end governance.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Lower run costs and faster product iteration translate into structural expense-ratio advantages for adopters.
insights.quote: Lower run costs because the unified agentic core requires fewer redundant layers for high availability
insights.locator: Some advantages of a unified agentic

insights.claim: Core-system vendors are already rolling out agentic capabilities: in August 2026 Guidewire introduced an agentic framework for insurers to build and run their own agents on the Guidewire Cloud Platform, and Duck Creek launched an agentic AI platform with an insurance-specific intelligence layer combining fine-tuned language models, machine learning and rule-based reasoning.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Insurance core-software vendors are racing to embed agentic AI to defend their platform position.
insights.quote: in August 2026, Guidewire introduced an agentic framework
insights.locator: Vendors that offer core system platforms

insights.claim: BCG argues insurers should not wait for vendors because vendor rollout may be too slow, first movers building operational and data foundations gain competitive advantage, and a general-purpose vendor platform will not include an insurer's own data ontology.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Suggests carriers keep strategic AI ownership in-house, potentially limiting how much of the agentic value pool core vendors capture.
insights.quote: A vendor platform built for general use won’t include an insurer’s own data ontology.
insights.locator: This activity might tempt insurers to

insights.claim: BCG states the window for insurers to shape what gets built in agentic core transformation will remain open for months, not years.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect accelerated core-modernization decisions and spending among insurers in the near term.
insights.quote: the window to shape what gets built will remain open for months, not years
insights.locator: For COOs, CIOs, and other technology

insights.claim: Without an orchestration layer, autonomous agents in insurance processes may contradict one another, duplicate efforts, or stall waiting for inputs no one anticipated providing.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Multi-agent deployments without orchestration carry operational risk; orchestration tooling is a necessary spend category.
insights.quote: autonomous agents may contradict one another, duplicate efforts, or stall
insights.locator: Without an orchestration layer, autonomous agents

insights.claim: BCG proposes a three-tier control hierarchy: an orchestrator meta-agent governing process flow and state, specialist agents with bounded autonomy over subprocesses such as FNOL, damage assessment, liability evaluation and reserve management, and subagents executing granular tasks like document extraction, API calls and reimbursement calculation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A reference architecture for evaluating insurance AI platforms and vendors.
insights.locator: Agentic orchestration addresses this through

insights.claim: The three-tier design allows agents to be reused across business units and lines of business, such as sharing a claims triage specialist agent, while supporting auditing at every stage gate and human oversight where compliance requires.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Agent reuse across lines of business creates scale economies favoring larger multi-line carriers.
insights.quote: an insurer can share a claims triage specialist agent across different lines of business
insights.locator: This three-tier design allows for

insights.claim: The process blueprint is an executable artifact and single point of configuration that defines process stages, stage-gate requirements, permitted agents and expected outputs, specifying where execution follows fixed rules and where agents have autonomy; it acts as the contract between business logic and agentic execution.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Mixing deterministic certified calculations with bounded agent autonomy is how regulated insurers can deploy agents auditably.
insights.quote: It serves as the contract between business logic and agentic execution.
insights.locator: Following the Process Blueprint

insights.claim: Without a shared data language, each agent speaks its own dialect, so data is transformed at every handoff, meaning is lost and errors propagate; e.g. a fraud agent must know a 'car' in a submission is the same 'vehicle' in registration data and 'auto' in a claim report.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Data semantics, not models, is the hidden failure point in multi-agent insurance systems.
insights.quote: each agent speaks its own dialect, giving different meanings to the same set of concepts
insights.locator: Tech leaders need to ensure all

insights.claim: An insurance ontology is a shared machine-readable representation of entities (policy, risk, claim, party, coverage, premium), their relationships, attributes and business rules, governed as code and evolving with the business and agent knowledge.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Ontology-building capability becomes a differentiating asset for carriers and a gap for generic vendor platforms.
insights.locator: Insurance ontology is the answer.

insights.claim: Because the ontology is deeply embedded in the core and constantly evolving, BCG argues it cannot easily be outsourced, making it one of two nondelegable decisions for tech leaders alongside architecture choice.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Limits the addressable market for outsourced AI/IT services and favors carriers with strong in-house data engineering.
insights.quote: it’s not something that can easily be outsourced
insights.locator: The ontology is a living data

insights.claim: A good ontology embeds compliance rules such as the EU's GDPR as data constraints, so an agent accessing personal data outside its scope is blocked by the structure of the data itself rather than an external firewall.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Compliance-by-design lowers regulatory risk of agentic AI deployment in regulated markets.
insights.quote: blocked not by an external firewall but by the structure of the data itself
insights.locator: Embedded Governance.

insights.claim: Reasoning over semantically rich ontology concepts rather than raw data improves agent reasoning quality and reduces hallucinations, and lets learning propagate across agents, e.g. insights from a motor fraud agent automatically reaching a property fraud agent via a shared 'claim fraud pattern' concept.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Shared ontologies create compounding cross-line learning effects, a potential scale advantage for early adopters.
insights.quote: Insights accumulated by a motor fraud detection agent propagate automatically to the property fraud detection agent
insights.locator: Continuous Improvement.
